ahara: Heavy, hot, unctuous, sweet and astringent foods in excess
Intake during acute fever of heavy foods
agantuja: Injury by weapon, brickbat, whip, wood, fist or teeth
Ill attachment with evil spirits or organisms

purvaroopa: Aversion to fire, sun, air and water
roopa: Pyrexia (excessive heat in body and mind)
Absence of perspiration (due to blocking of channels)
Heaviness in abdomen in ama stage
bheda: Seven types by location in dhatus
Eight types by etiology (vataja, pittaja, kaphaja, vata-pittaja, vata-kaphaja, pitta-kaphaja, sannipataja, agantuja)
diseases.sadhyata: Curable if caused by one dosa and recently arisen in strong patient without complication; maintainable if caused by two dosas; incurable if caused by three dosas with full symptoms

ahara: Intake of hot, sharp, sour, pungent and salty substances in excess

roopa: Bleeding from upper orifices (nose, mouth, ears, eyes) or lower orifices (rectum, urinary)
Viscous, pale, unctuous, slimy blood indicates Kapha association
Blackish, reddish, frothy, thin, rough blood indicates Vata type
Ochre-like, black, cow-urine-like, smoky, collyrium-like colour indicates Pitta type
bheda: Upward (urdhvaga) - through seven orifices in head
diseases.sadhyata: Curable if one passage and one dosa in strong patient without complication; maintainable if two dosas; incurable if all three dosas, exceedingly forceful, corpse-like smell, deeply emaciated patient

ahara: Excessive intake of rough food and drinks (vatika)
Pungent, sour, irritant, hot, burning, rough substances in excess (paittika)
Cold, heavy, unctuous food in excess (kaphaja)

roopa: Pain in cardiac region, navel, sides, abdomen and pelvis
Fever, thirst, reddishness on face and body, pain aggravating during digestion, sweating, burning, tenderness (paittika)
Feeling of weakness, cold fever, malaise, nausea, cough, anorexia, heaviness, coldness, mild pain, hardness with elevation (kaphaja)
bheda: Raktaja Gulma (in women - from accumulated menstrual blood)
Five sites: pelvic region, umbilical region, cardiac region, flanks
diseases.sadhyata: Incurable if intense pain, burning, stony hard, elevated, quickly inflaming, severe, with loss of strength of mind, body and agni; incurable if widely accumulated, deep-rooted, covered with veins, associated with fever, dyspnoea, vomiting, diarrhoea and swelling
